name: Bob Yobbo Junior

tenures.note: Won the inaugural LTD Championship at New Blood Rising (17 November 2001), defeating Barabbas, Scott Royal (twice) and Myrddin across the tournament. Lost the title to Venom at an uncaptured show before Winter's Wrath, and won a No-DQ #1 contender's rematch against Inferno Kid at that same Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) without recovering the belt.

tenures.source: the federation's own roleplay board and its served show documents (promotions/lcw-mercury/)

caption: Woke at four in the morning before a title defence, phoned his doctor, and won LTD's own inaugural championship the same tournament he was rattled by — later self-identified, in Mercury's own corpus, as Robert Young.

name: David Beaumont
caption: The president LCW's own roster pages ran the federation through, who fired his champion on the night of the split and built its roleplay half out of whoever stayed.

name: Gravity

tenures.role: wrestler — challenged for the World Heavyweight Championship
tenures.note: Billed for a World Title Match (special guest referee) against Pheonyx (c) on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001; the results page was never captured.

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Fought in Mercury's own TSC feud and Caged Carnage match; his own career ended there in a hardcore match against TR Saxton at Silent Nightmare (30 December 2001).

Evo's own co-owner alongside Edward Olmstead, "in the four months since Gravity had come to Evo"; billed in-fiction under his own name, "Gravity" (see this row's existing note on the coincidence clause). Weighs in on booking calls, e.g. adding Ruthless Johnny Righteous to the Impulse 2.1 four-way.

caption: Business partner of president David Beaumont, billed a World Title challenge against Pheonyx with a special guest referee in August 2001, and later carried the name into a hardcore-match dream pairing fans still remembered a year on.
notes: Billed in-fiction as this character's own name: "his co-owner and business partner, Tim Hall, known worldwide as LCW Hall of Famer Gravity" (promotions/lcw-mercury/archive/mercury-a-brief-history-of-mercury.html).

name: "Ruthless" Johnny Righteous

tenures.note: Billed defending the Universal Title against Pariah on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001; the results page was never captured. TR Saxton's 2002 Late Night Lethal interview (lcw-late-night-lethal-episode-4.html) recalls him returning to Evo to feud with Righteous.

Billed "Inactive" on the roster page before his in-ring return, months removed from LCW rings, at Impulse 2.1's Madhouse #1-contender four-way; the "Lifestyle" segment stages his own uneasy arrival at Club Evo's nightclub-styled venue as a culture shock.

caption: Defended the LCW Universal Heavyweight Championship against Pariah on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001, and was still being talked about as a rival a year later on Late Night Lethal.

identity.note: Shares the nickname Ruthless with an unrelated LOW wrestler billed "Ruthless"; no document names both, and a shared one-word nickname across unrelated federations is never a merge on its own.

name: Carlos Rodriguez

tenures.note: Billed teaming with Bob Yobbo Junior against The Birds on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001.

caption: Teamed with Bob Yobbo Junior against The Birds on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001; his own applause line in the LCW Late Night Lethal audience introduction of Doctor David Chambers suggests he was a recent arrival at the time.

name: Memosarks

tenures.note: Billed in a Debut Match against Scott Royal on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001; Harbinger's 2002 Late Night Lethal interview recalls wanting to face him "before he left".

tenures.role: wrestler — first Mercury North American Champion
tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Mercury's own first North American Champion, climbing a blood-soaked ladder at Rising; left with a collapsed lung by Oblivion in April 2002.

caption: Debuted against Scott Royal on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001, became LCW Mercury's first North American Champion that November, and had left the roster with a collapsed lung by the time Harbinger name-checked him fondly on Late Night Lethal the following year.

identity.note: Shares the distinctive name Memosarks with a WWA wrestler; no document names both, and a shared name across unrelated federations is never a merge on its own.

name: Scott Royal

tenures.note: Billed against Memosarks in a Debut Match on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001.

caption: Opposed Memosarks in a Debut Match on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001.

identity.note: Shares the name Scott Royal with an EWO wrestler; no document names both, and a shared name across unrelated federations is never a merge on its own.

name: Barabbas

tenures.note: Cited as an example roster name on the Superstars menu page ("How much does Barabbas weigh?").

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Carried a cross to the ring as half of Legion, and put Slingshot through a table at Mercury Rising.

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Barabbas and Myrddin wrestled as Legion in LTD's own first tournament (New Blood Rising, 17 November 2001), the same partnership already registered on this row's own lcw-mercury tenure. Held the LTD Lethal Championship by March 2002, defending it in a Hardcore Steel Cage against Sloan Malice.

caption: Named only as an example of the kind of vital statistic the roster pages could answer — how much Barabbas weighed — before surfacing as half of Legion in both LCW's developmental federation and Mercury, and LTD's own Lethal Champion by March 2002.

name: Bobby Borashi

tenures.note: "Senior Official Bobby Borashi", cited on the Superstars menu page's list of officials.
Refereed both of Doctor David Chambers' own Evo Title defenses read this pass (Impulse 1.9 v Brad Case, Dawning v Dean Wallace).

caption: LCW's Senior Official, named on the federation's own Superstars menu page.

name: Jessica Hernendez

tenures.role: interviewer — LCW Leading Ladies of Journalism
tenures.note: Named as an interviewer on the Superstars menu page and, alongside "Luscious" Leah Grant, as one of the "LCW Leading Ladies of Journalism" on the Members menu page's interview-request section.

caption: One of the LCW Leading Ladies of Journalism, fielding member interview requests alongside "Luscious" Leah Grant.

identity.note: Shares the given name Jessica with an unrelated WWA entity; no document names both.

name: "Luscious" Leah Grant

tenures.role: interviewer — LCW Leading Ladies of Journalism
tenures.note: Named alongside Jessica Hernendez as one of the "LCW Leading Ladies of Journalism" on the Members menu page's interview-request section.

caption: The other half of the LCW Leading Ladies of Journalism, alongside Jessica Hernendez.

name: KC Steele

tenures.note: "The widely recognized talents of play-by-play man KC Steele, Entertainment Weekly's 'Best Sports Announcer of 2000'" (Shows index, Sept 2001); billed as a Tempest host alongside "Iron" John Hughes on the 9 August 2001 card.

caption: Tempest's play-by-play voice, billed by the federation's own copy as Entertainment Weekly's "Best Sports Announcer of 2000".

identity.note: Shares the surname/nickname Steele with an unrelated UWF entity billed "Steel"; no document names both.

name: "Iron" John Hughes

tenures.note: Billed as KC Steele's "new partner, former Sportscenter announcer" on the Shows index of September 2001, and as a Tempest host on the 9 August 2001 card.

caption: KC Steele's broadcast partner on Tempest, billed as a former Sportscenter announcer.

name: "Your Idol" Isaac Leeds

tenures.note: "Hosted by 'Your Idol' Isaac Leeds and 'Coach' Jimmy Clark" (Shows menu, October 2001).

caption: Co-hosted LCW Weekly, the federation's own recap show, alongside "Coach" Jimmy Clark.

name: "Coach" Jimmy Clark

tenures.note: "Hosted by 'Your Idol' Isaac Leeds and 'Coach' Jimmy Clark" (Shows menu, October 2001).

caption: Co-hosted LCW Weekly alongside "Your Idol" Isaac Leeds.

identity.note: Shares the given name Jimmy with an unrelated ACW wrestler billed "The Jimmy"; no document names both.

name: Joe Black

tenures.note: Hosted the December 2001 edition of Black Talk in character, firing T.R. Saxton on air (then walking it back), and needling Rook, the Gol, Apex, Pariah and Used with on-air questions.

tenures.source: promotions/lcw-evo/archive/evo-officials.html; the federation's own served show segments (promotions/lcw-evo/)
tenures.note: Evo's own Vice President, Talent Relations, and play-by-play commentator alongside Olivia Heimdal on every read show segment.
Dated from the fed's own appearance record (15 shows: matches, officiating, segments). Widened by its own roleplay (2003-04-11).

caption: Hosted Black Talk in character, a Tequila-labelled coffee mug in hand, complaining about the job and taking swings at half the roster along the way.
notes: Jokes on-air that he and Rook "have the same last name"; the fed's own text never states the two are related and none is asserted here. The security team sent to fetch him at ringside during Rook Black's hand injury (see rook-black-lcw-evo's own tenure) is the first direct confirmation, beyond the on-air joke about sharing a surname, that Joe Black is Rook Black's own father: "Find his Dad!... Fortunately, Joe found him" (promotions/lcw-evo/rp/rp-shock-and-extraction.html).

name: Angel Teves

tenures.note: "Angel's relationship with LCW is terminated", per Joe Black's Black Talk of December 2001.

caption: Released from LCW in December 2001, per Joe Black's own on-air announcement on Black Talk.

identity.note: Shares the generic gimmick word Angel (or the aka Angel) with unrelated entities in four other federations; no document names any of them together, and a shared generic word is never a merge on its own.

name: T.R. Saxton

tenures.note: "Falsely" fired and unfired on Black Talk, December 2001. Interviewed on Late Night Lethal Episode 4 (c. 2002), where he gives his kayfabe "real name" as Jason Downer, a joke on his own gimmick name honoring Theodore Roosevelt; started the Evo/Mercury split in Mercury and returned to Evo to feud with Johnny Righteous.

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Put Harbinger through a Squeaky Clean I Quit gauntlet before quitting Mercury on camera in February 2002 ("I quit, you soulless bastards... see you in Philly"), matching this row's own already-noted return to Evo to feud with Johnny Righteous.

Dawning's own "Mystery Opponent," billed as the first wrestler to cross over between the Mercury/Evo split; lost to Used by DQ. Cut a "Legend?" promo at Impulse 2.1 dismissing Evo's own claimed legends before Used ambushed him; a since-unaired Impulse 2.2 was set to pit him against Ruthless Johnny Righteous.

caption: A recurring undercard target of Joe Black's jokes on Black Talk, and by 2002 a returning Evo wrestler telling Late Night Lethal that his gimmick name is a Teddy Roosevelt joke played straight.

name: Dexter Riot

tenures.note: Named alongside Inferno Kid as an upcoming pairing Joe Black says he isn't looking forward to, on Black Talk, December 2001.

caption: Booked opposite Inferno Kid in a pairing Joe Black publicly dreaded on Black Talk, December 2001.

name: Inferno Kid

tenures.note: Named alongside Dexter Riot as an upcoming pairing Joe Black says he isn't looking forward to, on Black Talk, December 2001.

identity.note: Shares part of a name with inferno-lcw-mercury, a separately-billed Mercury wrestler; the two names are treated as distinct pending a document naming both.

caption: Booked opposite Dexter Riot in a pairing Joe Black publicly dreaded on Black Talk, December 2001.

name: Dante Anderson

tenures.note: "The office reports having exceptionally cooperative behavior from Dante Anderson" and may be un-benched for television, per Black Talk, December 2001; a Tempest show title from the same window ("Tempest: Dante Loses It; The Texan Saves the Inmate", 28 July 2001) also names a "Dante".

caption: A wrestler under office discipline in late 2001, per Joe Black's own Black Talk report that his television time might be restored.

identity.note: Shares the surname Anderson or the given name Dante with unrelated wrestlers in three other federations; no document names any of them together.

name: Gol

tenures.note: Addressed as "the Gol" on Black Talk, December 2001; named among the fed's own consensus top roleplayers in the Roleplay Tips document of January 2002; went on to hold the Mercury World Championship by May 2002, per LCW Central Forums.

tenures.role: wrestler — Mercury World Champion; Oblivion co-founder
tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Founded Oblivion with Magnum Wolf at Pariah's own expense on 11 March 2002, and won the Mercury World Heavyweight Championship at Suicide.

caption: Went from a Joe Black punchline on Black Talk in 2001 to one of the fed's own consensus top roleplayers by January 2002, held the Mercury North American Championship for a week that March, and won the Mercury World Championship in May.

name: Lex Laww

tenures.note: "After putting my character Lex Laww on the shelf" — the Roleplay Tips document's own author, LCW's co-head booker, used Lex Laww as his worked example throughout (height 6'3", weight 245 lbs, olive skin, black police-style fatigues, Kevlar vest, silver Oakley sunglasses). Entered EHW (LCW's own predecessor federation) against a wrestler billed Big Pee-On; a Silent Nightmare PPV show title of 23 December 2000 ("Lex Laww's Last Stand") and a Tempest show title of 26 April 2001 ("Hello, Joe; Farewell, Lex") bracket a run through LCW's classic era; Harbinger's 2002 Late Night Lethal interview recalls missing "all the ring rats Lex attracted" from the Evo side of the split.

caption: LCW's co-head booker used his own character, the Italian, sunglasses-and-fatigues Lex Laww, as the worked example throughout the fed's official Roleplay Tips document — a main eventer in three federations by his own account, on the shelf by January 2002.
notes: No lcw-evo tenure added on mention alone.

name: Archangel

tenures.note: Named among the fed's own consensus top roleplayers consulted for the Roleplay Tips document, January 2002.

caption: One of the roleplayers LCW's own official tips document named as the fed's consensus best, January 2002.

identity.note: Shares the generic archangel gimmick name with entities in five unrelated federations; a shared archetype name across unrelated feds is never a merge on its own.

name: Blayd

tenures.note: Named among the fed's own consensus top roleplayers for the Roleplay Tips document (January 2002); a Tuesday Tempest show title of 14 November 2000 ("Blayd Triumphant") and the LCW Central Forums "LCW supercard" thread (dated to his own October 2000 run) both place him in LCW's classic era.

caption: Won on the second Tuesday Tempest of the federation's own life, in November 2000, and was still named a consensus top roleplayer by January 2002.

name: Hector Carreras

tenures.note: Named among the fed's own consensus top roleplayers (Roleplay Tips, January 2002); the same document recalls him "formerly La Mosca" returning to the fed as a face after "such a big heel character", challenged over his integrity in a promo by the character of Pheonyx.

caption: Returned to the fed as a face under his own name after a heel run as the masked La Mosca, in a turn the fed's own Roleplay Tips document cites as one of its best-remembered angles.

name: Mike Static

tenures.note: Named among the fed's own consensus top roleplayers as "Mike Static" (Roleplay Tips, January 2002); a No Remorse PPV show title of 4 March 2001 ("Static Ascendant") places a title win in LCW's classic era, and the LCW supercard nostalgia thread pairs him against Pheonyx as "psychotic/athletic heels" from a July–December 2000 window.

Named on the Evo roster; a hospital-room encounter with Duel/Alex Lawson on 13 December 2001 re-triggered Lawson's own dissociative break (see duel-lcw-evo's own tenure), an event that both "Solitude" and Dawning's own "Champions" segment tie directly to Static's past career and eventual decline.

caption: Ascended at the No Remorse pay-per-view in March 2001 and was still a consensus top roleplayer named in the fed's own official tips document a year later.

identity.note: Shares the bare ring name Static with an NAPW wrestler; no document names both, and a shared one-word name across unrelated federations is never a merge on its own.

name: Used

tenures.note: Cited as an example roster name on the Superstars menu page ("Where is Used's hometown?"); named among the fed's own consensus top roleplayers (Roleplay Tips, January 2002); T.R. Saxton's 2002 Late Night Lethal interview recalls a bloody feud with him "last summer".
Won Dawning's Match 2 by disqualification over TR Saxton after his own pregnant wife Ophelia was thrown down; ambushed TR Saxton again in "Legend?" at Impulse 2.1, brawling him into the crowd.

caption: Named on the federation's own Superstars menu page as an example roster entry, and still a consensus top roleplayer and a fondly-recalled feud partner a year later.

name: Sickness

tenures.note: Harbinger's 2002 Late Night Lethal interview recalls having "been somewhat attached to Sickness" (denied as anything more); the LCW Central Forums "LCW supercard" nostalgia thread proposes "Frank & Liv Heimdal vs Joe Black & Sickness" as a dream tag match.

tenures.role: wrestler; authority-figure — revealed as Oblivion's own leader
tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Harbinger's own on-and-off partner across the held record; revealed on air as Oblivion's own leader on 5 April 2002, then beat David Beaumont in Suicide's own mixed-match opener.

caption: Rumoured, and denied, to have been involved with Harbinger; imagined by fans a year later as Joe Black's own tag partner on a wished-for reunion card.

name: Aaron Antioch

tenures.note: Interviewed on Late Night Lethal (dated 21 May 2001 in the source, though its own references to the Suicide pay-per-view and the office holding owner David Beaumont hostage read as later than that byline — see the show's own registry note). Formerly billed "the Apostle", one half of the tag team Divine Intervention with his cousin (billed there as Angel); switched gimmicks after Angel took time off to marry Danielle, and by the interview wrestled under a new ring name the show itself never states on air, referring to it only as a past-tense change from "the Apostle".

Wrestles as "Lost" in Evo — confirmed the same man directly inside the wing's own record, not merely presumed: Duel's own "Champions" monologue ("Michael and Aaron and I... Aaron had failed in his match against Gryfon") and Michael Gabrielle's own on-air line in "Messiah's Challenge" ("who among us should go after you, didn't we Aaron?", addressed directly to Lost) both name him. Lost teamed with Michael Gabrielle as the Tribulation Saints (won at Impulse 1.9 over Pheonyx/Gryfon), lost the Dawning roof submission match to Gryfon, and is billed opposite Doctor David Chambers on the never-captured 13 December 2001 card. "Lost" is deliberately NOT added to aka[] — this row's own pre-existing note already flagged the exact same auto-link risk a common English word carries (see CURATION.md and scripts/cross-reference.mjs's EXCLUDE_NAMES discipline); the identification stays in prose.

caption: Wrestled as the religious-gimmick Apostle in the tag team Divine Intervention before switching gimmicks when his cousin and tag partner took time off to marry — the same interview that recaps it declines to say the new name on air.
notes: It is not recorded as an aka here for that reason; a future EXCLUDE_NAMES addition to scripts/cross-reference.mjs would allow it to be added safely. This pass's own Evo-corpus read ("Father's Day Comes Early This Year") adds his own kayfabe birth name in full: Matthew Green, son of convicted murderer James Green (his mother Eileen's killer, up for parole) — visited in prison at East Jersey State Prison, Rahway NJ, still refusing forgiveness. Distinct from the "cousin"/"nephew" wording inconsistency Michael Gabrielle's own tenure below flags.

name: Olivia Heimdal

tenures.note: Billed opposite Joe Black & Sickness alongside her brother Frank as "Frank & Liv Heimdal" in the LCW Central Forums supercard nostalgia thread; a later poster there calls the pairing "the Heimdal siblings"; her face appears on the video wall behind Frank Heimdal's own Madhouse Championship match at Evo's Dawning (see frank-heimdal-lcw-evo). TR Saxton's 2002 Late Night Lethal interview names an "Olivia" he wanted to face.

tenures.source: promotions/lcw-evo/archive/evo-officials.html; the federation's own served show segments and Legends Board (promotions/lcw-evo/)
tenures.note: Evo's own color commentator alongside Joe Black on every read show segment (billed "Livvie" on-air), separately from her billed appearance behind Frank Heimdal's Dawning match. A documented romantic relationship with Duel/Alex Lawson ("Solitude," a voicemail: "when we started this relationship, it wasn't meant to be like this") ends sometime before Dawning; she takes in a convalescing Doctor David Chambers at her own house afterward ("Life at the Heimdals Part 1").

caption: Frank Heimdal's sister and periodic tag partner, written by the same handler as the Heimdal siblings.

name: Big Pee-On

tenures.note: "The first title contender Lex Laww went after when he entered EHW" (Roleplay Tips, January 2002) — EHW being LCW's own unheld predecessor federation. A poster's own nostalgia dating in the LCW supercard thread places a Big Pee-On appearance in October 2000, LCW's own founding month; the exact promotion the EHW-era feud took place in is not established by either document.

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents and roleplay board (promotions/lcw-mercury/)
tenures.note: Powerwalked out as Beaumont's own surprise North American Title challenger and lasted barely two minutes against Geoffrey Slate (22 February 2002).

caption: Lex Laww's first title challenger on record, from a feud a fan's own decade-later memory dates to LCW's founding month of October 2000.

name: Bear the Bear

tenures.note: A worn childhood teddy bear that Doctor David Chambers speaks through as a full stable member, billed by name on Late Night Lethal's own guest introduction ("The Asylum: Lost, The Doctor, and Bear the Bear!").
Doctor David Chambers' own stuffed-bear stable member/weapon throughout Evo, credited by name on the managers/valets listing; connects at Dawning with the finisher Steelhead.

caption: A stuffed animal billed as a full member of The Asylum, spoken through by Doctor David Chambers on television.
notes: Staged, not appearance-based, per the nonhuman datatype's own doctrine.

name: Steve Lieberman

tenures.note: Hosted both surviving editions of Late Night Lethal, the federation's own late-night talk-show parody, opening each with a mock biography sketch and a running gag that he is, off-camera, sleeping with his own co-host.

caption: Hosted Late Night Lethal in the mould of a talk-show egomaniac, opening the surviving episodes with a mock biography and a running bit that the show barely holds together.

identity.note: Shares the bare first name Steve with unrelated entities in two other federations; no document names any of them together, and a shared common first name is never a merge on its own.

name: Ashley Mendel

tenures.note: Steve Lieberman's co-host on both surviving Late Night Lethal editions, seated on the show's own guest couch.

caption: Steve Lieberman's long-suffering co-host on Late Night Lethal, billed "The Dream" Mendel.

name: Sacapuntas Jones

tenures.note: The unseen announcer voice on both surviving Late Night Lethal editions, introducing Steve Lieberman and the guests.

caption: The unseen announcer voice that opens every surviving edition of Late Night Lethal.

name: Prince of Space

tenures.note: A costumed, disoriented gimmick wrestler, previously the subject of a "memorable two-part series" with Doctor David Chambers and Aaron Antioch, per Steve Lieberman on Late Night Lethal Episode 4; his surprise reappearance there ends in a comic showdown with a costumed "Phantom of Krankor" and a squirt-gun standoff.

caption: A masked, gimmick-costumed wrestler whose surprise return on Late Night Lethal Episode 4 dissolved into a squirt-gun showdown with a rival called Phantom of Krankor.
